title: Dorian Finney-Smith Recalls the Night the Luka Doncic Trade Broke
htmlContent:
Few trades in NBA history landed with the force of the February 2025 deal that sent Luka Doncic to the Los Angeles Lakers and Anthony Davis to the Dallas Mavericks. Dorian Finney-Smith had a better seat for it than almost anyone. He was a Laker, a teammate of Davisand a longtime former teammate of Doncic.Now a member of the Atlanta Hawks, Finney-Smith recently shared with LandonBuford.com what that night looked like from the inside.

A Big Win at the Garden

Finney-Smith had only been in Los Angeles for about six weeks. The Brooklyn Nets traded him to the Lakers in late December 2024, and he quickly became a key wing in JJ Redick's rotation. On Feb. 1, 2025, the Lakers rolled into Madison Square Garden and beat the Knicks 128-112 behind a LeBron James triple-double of 33 points, 12 assists and 11 rebounds.

"Oh man, I was with the Lakers by then, since I'd come over from Brooklyn," Finney-Smith said. "We were in New York and had just beaten the Knicks. Great win. I was with AD after the game, and we were talking about getting together to celebrate. A couple of nights in New York. Then around 12 o'clock, the trade news hit."

Davis, the man he had just been making plans with, was suddenly headed to Dallas.

The Trade Nobody Saw Coming

ESPN first reported the three-team deal shortly after midnight Eastern time. Los Angeles received Doncic, Maxi Kleber and Markieff Morris. Dallas got Davis, Max Christie and a 2029 first-round pick, while Utah took Jalen Hood-Schifino and two second-round picks. The Mavericks had dealt away a 25-year-old, five-time All-NBA First Team guard who had led them to the NBA Finals just eight months earlier.

There had been no leaks and no rumors, and the reaction around the league was disbelief. Finney-Smith felt it immediately.

"It was a shock. Everybody was texting me," he said. "I texted Luka just to see what the truth was. He was probably busy, so he got back to me the next day. I figured Luka's phone was going crazy, so I called Max [Christie]. Max was calm, and we were talking like, 'Is this real?' Then it got confirmed the next day."

A Bond Built in Dallas

Finney-Smith's connection to Doncic runs deep. After going undrafted out of Florida in 2016, he signed with the Mavericks and spent nearly seven seasons in Dallas. He developed into a dependable 3-and-D forward and became one of Doncic's most trusted teammates from the moment the Slovenian star arrived in 2018.

The two were central pieces of the 2022 Mavericks team that reached the Western Conference Finals. Finney-Smith was then traded to Brooklyn in February 2023 as part of the Kyrie Irvingdeal, but the relationship stayed strong. That history made him one of the first people Doncic connected with as he processed the move.

Helping Luka Settle In

"When I talked to Luka, we talked for a while," Finney-Smith said. "It was good that I was already there, so he wasn't walking into a completely new situation. It was a smooth transition."

For a player who had expected to spend his entire career in Dallas, finding a familiar face in the Lakers locker room mattered. Doncic joined a roster that also added Kleber, another former Mavericks teammate, giving him a small circle of trusted voices in a brand-new city.

From Los Angeles to Atlanta

Finney-Smith's own journey has kept moving since then. He signed with the Houston Rockets in the summer of 2025 but saw limited action, appearing in 37 games and averaging 3.3 points. Houston traded him to the Charlotte Hornets in July 2026 along with three second-round picks. In September, Charlotte flipped him to Atlanta for Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash.

Now in his 11th NBA season, Finney-Smith brings the Hawks size on the wing, defensive versatility and a veteran voice. He has played alongside some of the biggest names of his era and has been close to several of the league's biggest moments.

A Night He Won't Forget

Plenty of players have stories about where they were when big news broke. Finney-Smith's is unusual because he stood at the center of both sides of it. He was with Davis when the news hit, and he was the familiar face waiting for Doncic in Los Angeles. A celebration in New York turned into a night that changed the league, and he watched it unfold in real time.
excerpt: Dorian Finney-Smith, now with the Atlanta Hawks, shared with LandonBuford.com what it was like to be inside the moment the February 2025 Luka Doncic–Anthony Davis trade broke — standing next to Davis in New York when the news hit shortly after midnight.
